It is, of course, also possible to render προλαμβάνω in ⟦Galatians 6:1|Galatians 6:1⟧ as ‘to be involved in.’ Compare Domain 90K.

The most generic expression for prayer may simply be ‘to speak to God.’ It is normally best to avoid an expression which means primarily ‘to recite.’

There may also be important distinctions on the basis of urgency and need. The most generic expression for prayer may simply be ‘to speak to God.’ It is normally best to avoid an expression which means primarily ‘to recite.’

The difference implied in the presumed force or strength required frequently results in quite different words being used.|The phrase προσλαμβάνομαι τροφῆς (⟦Acts 27:36|Acts 27:36⟧) may be interpreted as an idiom meaning ‘to eat’ (see footnote at μετέχω LN 23.2).

s.d: to strike suddenly and with force
s.g: to strike against; to burst against
s.c: It is also possible to understand προσρήγνυμι in ⟦Luke 6:48|Luke 6:48⟧ as meaning ‘to overflow the stream bed,’ but in view of the occurrence of τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, the meaning of ‘strike against’ seems more justified.

s.d: to give detailed instructions as to what must be done{N:001}
s.g: to order; to instruct; to tell; to command

s.dp: Arrange, Organize › Organize [of events and states]
s.d: to arrange in a prescribed manner
s.g: to prescribe; to arrange for
s.c: In some languages it may be important to recast to some extent the rendering of the second part of ⟦Acts 17:26|Acts 17:26⟧ so as to combine both place and time, for example, ‘he set limits to the time and determined the places they would dwell.’

s.d: (derivative of {L:προΐστημι<SDBG:προΐστημι:000001>}[b] ‘to be active in helping,’ {D:35.12}) a woman who is active in helping
s.g: helper; patroness (in the sense of one engaged in supporting an individual or endeavor)

s.d: to add something to an existing quantity
s.g: to add
s.c: In a number of languages it is not at all difficult to speak of ‘adding things,’ but to add events may provide some special difficulties in restructuring. For example, in ⟦Luke 3:20|Luke 3:20⟧ it may be important to translate as ‘he had done many other bad things, but he also did this,’ and in ⟦Galatians 2:6|Galatians 2:6⟧ it may be helpful to translate ‘for those who were of repute did not say that I should do anything more than I was doing.’

s.d: to place something at the disposal of someone else
s.g: to give; to provide; to grant

s.d: (a Semitic idiom, literally: to place with his fathers) to carry out a burial procedure
s.g: to bury

s.d: to continue, with focus upon the next element
s.g: to continue; to proceed to

s.d: to mark an immediately following event
s.g: to proceed to

s.d: to run into the presence of someone
s.g: to run up to; to run into the presence of

s.d: the flesh of fish as food{N:001}
s.g: fish
s.c: In literature outside the NT, προσφάγιον normally refers to some type of relish eaten with bread, but in ⟦John 21:5|John 21:5⟧ (the only occurrence in the NT) the reference is to the flesh of fish.

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › New, Old [primarily non-temporal]
s.d: pertaining to what is new and recent, in the sense of not previously existing
s.g: new; recent; new and different

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: pertaining to a point of time preceding another point of time, but with a relatively short interval
s.g: recently
s.c: For languages which do not have an adverb meaning ‘recently,’ one can always introduce an equivalent approximate statement in ⟦Acts 18:2|Acts 18:2⟧, for example, ‘he met a Jew who only a few days before had come from Italy.’ One cannot be certain as to the interval of time, but a phrase such as ‘a few days before’ can be a satisfactory equivalent.

s.d: to carry or bring something into the presence of someone, usually implying a transfer of something to that person
s.g: to carry to; to bring (to)

s.d: to bring or lead into the presence of someone
s.g: to lead before; to bring into the presence of; to bring to

s.d: to present something to someone, often involving actual physical transport of the object in question
s.g: to bring to; to present to

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Behavior, Conduct
s.d: to behave or act in a particular way with respect to someone
s.g: to behave toward; to deal with; to do to; to act

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
s.d: pertaining to that which causes people to be pleased with something
s.g: pleasing; lovely

s.d: that which is offered to God in religious activity
s.g: offering; sacrifice

s.d: to address an audience, with possible emphasis upon loudness
s.g: to address; to speak out to

s.d: to call out, with the probable implication of seeking some response
s.g: to call out to

s.d: to call to, with a possible implication of a reciprocal relation
s.g: to call; to call to

s.dp: Activities Involving Liquids or Masses › Movement of Liquids or Masses
s.d: the act of pouring something on or against something
s.g: pouring (or possibly sprinkling)
s.c: Since in most contexts this act of πρόσχυσις τοῦ αἵματος is spoken of as ‘sprinkling,’ it may be preferable to employ ‘sprinkling’ in ⟦Hebrews 11:28|Hebrews 11:28⟧, since πρόσχυσις may have acquired a generic sense which would include the specific act of sprinkling. See also LN 47.16.

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › Touch, Feel
s.d: to touch something lightly, normally with the finger or hand
s.g: to touch
s.c: For another interpretation of προσψαύω in ⟦Luke 11:46|Luke 11:46⟧, see LN 18.11. Note that προσψαύω differs in meaning from προσψαύω ‘to touch’ (LN 18.11) in that it is understood in a hyperbolic sense of ‘to merely touch,’ while προσψαύω implies ‘doing something to help’ or ‘doing something about it.’

s.d: to touch something, with the intent of doing something about it
s.g: to touch; to touch to help
s.c: In employing a term for ‘touch’ in ⟦Luke 11:46|Luke 11:46⟧, it is important to use an expression which will imply ‘touching in order to relieve the burden.’ This may be done in some instances by translating ‘to help by touching’ or ‘to touch with a finger in order to help a little.’ For another interpretation of προσψαύω in ⟦Luke 11:46|Luke 11:46⟧, see LN 24.75.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Show Favoritism, Prejudice
s.d: to make unjust distinctions between people by treating one person better than another
s.g: to show favoritism; to be partial; partiality
s.c: ‘To show favoritism’ or ‘to be partial’ is expressed in an idiomatic manner in some languages, for example, ‘to look only upon a person’s face,’ ‘to call a sparrow a chicken,’ or ‘to give one’s clansman the best piece of meat.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Show Favoritism, Prejudice
s.d: (derivative of {L:προσωπολημπτέω<SDBG:προσωπολημπτέω:000000>} ‘to show favoritism,’ {D:88.238}) one who unjustly treats one person better than another
s.g: one who shows favoritism; a respecter of persons

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Show Favoritism, Prejudice
s.d: to make unjust distinctions between people by treating one person better than another
s.g: to show favoritism; to be partial; partiality
s.c: ‘To show favoritism’ or ‘to be partial’ is expressed in an idiomatic manner in some languages, for example, ‘to look only upon a person’s face,’ ‘to call a sparrow a chicken,’ or ‘to give one’s clansman the best piece of meat.’

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.d: the front part of the human head
s.g: face

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:πρόσωπον<SDBG:πρόσωπον:000000>}[a] face, {D:8.18})
s.g: person; individual

s.dp: Features of Objects › Two-Dimensional and Three-Dimensional Shapes
s.d: the two-dimensional surface of an object
s.g: surface; face
s.c: In a number of cases one does not translate πρόσωπον in the sense of ‘surface’ since it is an implied component of other terms. For example, the phrase ‘on the earth’ implies the surface of the earth.

s.d: the form or characteristics of something as seen
s.g: appearance

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:πρόσωπον<SDBG:πρόσωπον:000000>}[a] ‘face,’ {D:8.18}) the personal presence of an individual at a particular place
s.g: presence; being at a place

s.dp: Spacial Positions › In Front Of, Face To Face, In Back Of, Behind
s.d: a position in front of an object, whether animate or inanimate, which is regarded as having a spacial orientation of front and back{N:001}
s.g: in front of; before

s.dp: Spacial Positions › In Front Of, Face To Face, In Back Of, Behind
s.d: (an idiom, literally: face to face) the position of one person facing another, with the implication of direct, personal interaction
s.g: face to face
s.c: The implication of this idiom in ⟦1 Corinthians 13:12|1 Corinthians 13:12⟧ is that there will be clear understanding, and in some languages it is necessary to shift somewhat the figurative expression. For example, it may be necessary to render this passage as ‘how we now understand is like seeing a dim image in a mirror, but then we shall understand as clearly as though we were seeing face to face’ or ‘… as though we were seeing something directly.’

s.dp: Think › To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to see into the face) to judge on the basis of external appearances
s.g: to judge on the basis of appearance; to render a superficial judgment; to pay no attention to a person’s status; to judge on the basis of reputation
s.c: In some languages an equivalent of this expression in ⟦Matthew 22:16|Matthew 22:16⟧ may be ‘when you judge, you look into a man’s heart’ or ‘when you judge you see more than a person’s face’ or ‘when you judge a person, who he appears to be doesn’t count.’

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: (an idiom, literally: before the face, equivalent in meaning to {L:πρό<SDBG:πρό:000001>}[b] ‘before,’ {D:67.17}, but a somewhat more elaborate phrase rhetorically) a point of time, possibly only a short time before another point of time
s.g: before; previous

s.d: (a Semitic idiom, literally: to fix one’s face) to make a decision, with emphasis upon finality
s.g: to decide firmly; to resolve; to make up one’s mind definitely
s.c: In order to express the meaning of ‘to decide firmly,’ it may be useful in some instances to translate ‘to decide and to refuse to change one’s mind’ or ‘to decide and not to change.’

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Suppose, Think Possible
s.d: (an idiom, literally: those things according to the face) that which seems to be so
s.g: outward appearance; what things seem to be

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Show Favoritism, Prejudice
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to take face) to make unjust distinctions between people by treating one person better than another
s.g: to show favoritism; to be partial; partiality
s.c: ‘To show favoritism’ or ‘to be partial’ is expressed in an idiomatic manner in some languages, for example, ‘to look only upon a person’s face,’ ‘to call a sparrow a chicken,’ or ‘to give one’s clansman the best piece of meat.’

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to admire the face) to praise someone, normally in an exaggerated or false manner and with insincere purpose{N:002}
s.g: to flatter

s.d: to stretch out or to spread out an object
s.g: to stretch out
s.c: In a number of languages one would not speak of a person being ‘stretched out’ in order to be whipped, but merely ‘tied up’ or ‘tied in a stretched-out position.’

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: pertaining to a point of time earlier in a sequence{N:001}
s.g: before; former; formerly

s.d: first, with the implication of emphasis, frequently in reference to time
s.g: the first time
s.c: It is also possible to understand πρότερος in ⟦Galatians 4:13|Galatians 4:13⟧ as meaning ‘earlier, formerly’ (see LN 67.18).

s.dp: Think › To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
s.d: to formulate a future course of action{N:001}
s.g: to plan beforehand; to purpose; to intend

s.d: to cause a manifest state or condition of someone or something
s.g: to cause to be; to bring forth; to offer

s.d: to urge a particular course of action
s.g: to urge

s.d: to run ahead of someone else, with the implication of arriving at a destination sooner
s.g: to run in front of; to run ahead of

s.d: to exist prior to some temporal reference point
s.g: to exist formerly; to be formerly

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Hypocrisy, Pretense
s.d: to pretend to be engaged in a particular activity
s.g: to pretend; pretense

s.d: what is said in defense of a particular action, but without real justification
s.g: excuse
s.c: In a number of languages ‘to have no excuse’ is rendered as ‘to not be able to justify’ or ‘to not be able to give a good reason for.’

s.d: to cause to exist in an evident manner
s.g: to cause to exist clearly; to bring forth; to produce

s.d: an utterance inspired by God
s.g: inspired utterance; prophecy
s.c: It is possible that προφητεία in ⟦1 Corinthians 13:8|1 Corinthians 13:8⟧ refers to the action of producing such inspired utterances rather than to the resulting verbal form of the utterances themselves.

s.d: the capacity or ability to utter inspired messages
s.g: to prophesy; ability to prophesy; to be able to speak inspired messages

s.d: to speak under the influence of divine inspiration, with or without reference to future events
s.g: to prophesy; to make inspired utterances

s.d: one who proclaims inspired utterances on behalf of God{N:001}
s.g: prophet; inspired preacher
s.c: There is a tendency in a number of languages to translate προφήτης only in the sense of ‘one who foretells the future,’ but foretelling the future was only a relatively minor aspect of the prophet’s function, though gradually it became more important. Patristic authors defined the function of a prophet mainly in terms of foretelling the future. In New Testament times, however, the focus was upon the inspired utterance proclaimed on behalf of and on the authority of God. Accordingly, in a number of languages it is more appropriate to translate προφήτης as ‘one who speaks for God.’

s.d: the writings of the prophets, including both the earlier and the later prophets{N:002}
s.g: the writings of the prophets; the Prophets
s.c: It is quite impossible in many languages to speak of ‘the Prophets’ in reference to the writings of the prophets, and therefore one must often say ‘what the prophets wrote’ or ‘the books containing the words of the prophets.’

s.d: (an idiom, literally: the Law and the Prophets) all of the sacred writings of the OT, including the Law, the Prophets, and the Writings{N:003}
s.g: the sacred writings; the Law and the Prophets

s.d: pertaining to divinely inspired utterances
s.g: prophetic; of the prophets

s.d: a woman who proclaims inspired utterances on behalf of God{N:001}
s.g: prophetess; inspired preacher

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: to do something at a point of time which immediately precedes another point of time
s.g: to be ahead of; to anticipate; to be in advance
s.c: It would also be possible to render this expression in ⟦Matthew 17:25|Matthew 17:25⟧ as ‘Jesus spoke to Simon before Simon could speak to him.’
